FEMA's advice for making a home safer from wildfire: use fire-resistant materials to build, renovate or make repairs. Find an outdoor water source with a hose that can reach any area of your property. results.text: FI-10 Before a wildfire: warnings, evacuation routes and supplies. FEMA's advice for preparing before a wildfire: sign up for your community's warning system. Know your community's evacuation routes, find several ways to leave the area, drive the evacuation routes and find shelter locations, and have a plan for pets and livestock. Gather emergency supplies, including N95 respirator masks that filter out particles in the air, and keep in mind each person's specific needs, including medication and the needs of pets. results.text: FI-02 Fires affect buildings unevenly, and damage may not be visible. Pour anticiper et protéger son habitation contre les feux de forêt, la page du ministère français conseille de stocker le bois et les bouteilles de gaz dans un abri fermé, éloigné de l'habitation ; avant l'été, de débroussailler autour de la maison en coupant la végétation basse et en élaguant les arbres pour qu'ils ne se touchent pas, afin d'éviter que le feu n'atteigne l'habitation, ce qui est une obligation dans les zones à risque ; et, dans une zone couverte par un plan de prévention du risque de feu de forêt, d'adapter la maison (volets, gouttières, toiture, aération). Selon la page, 90 % des maisons détruites lors des feux de forêt ne sont pas, ou sont mal, débroussaillées. Source: Ministère français de la Transition écologique, page Ayons les bons réflexes face aux feux de forêt et de végétation (mise à jour 3 juin 2026), web page retrieved 2026-10-16. results.text: FI-14 Début d'incendie : alerter, se protéger, s'informer. Si vous êtes témoin d'un début d'incendie, donnez l'alerte aux services de secours et essayez de localiser le feu. En attendant l'intervention des secours, mettez-vous à l'abri dans une habitation débroussaillée : la voiture n'est pas un abri sûr car elle pourrait brûler. Restez informé de la situation et suivez les consignes des secours ou de la mairie. Source: Ministère français de la Transition écologique, page Ayons les bons réflexes face aux feux de forêt et de végétation (mise à jour 3 juin 2026), web page retrieved 2026-10-16. results.text: FI-02 Fires affect buildings unevenly, and damage may not be visible. After a fire or wildfire, some structures can be burned so badly that they are essentially destroyed while others are untouched, simply because of the path of the fire. A fire can be limited to one building or affect a wide region. Heat can degrade structural members in ways that are not obvious: for example, the metal connector plates of wood trusses can be significantly affected by heat without any significant visible charring of the wood. Rapid evaluations have no effective method for judging intact members exposed to fire. Source: FEMA P-2055, Post-disaster Building Safety Evaluation Guidance (2019), PDF pages 61, 62. Origin of the sources: US. Audience: professional. Type: taken from the sources.

results.text: FI-04 Soot, fumes and who is most at risk. Toxicity of soot and fumes near active burning depends on what is burning, wind direction and speed, and the concentration and size of the particles. Burning plastics common in household furnishings produce highly toxic soot. People with heart or lung conditions, the elderly, smokers and children may be most affected. Evaluators of burned buildings can also be exposed to latent chemical hazards from products of combustion. Source: FEMA P-2055, Post-disaster Building Safety Evaluation Guidance (2019), PDF pages 62, 88. Origin of the sources: US. Audience: public. Type: taken from the sources. ## FI-05 Staying indoors during a smoke episode (smoke only, not approaching flames) Smoke exposure, not flame danger: during a smoke episode, a common advisory is to stay indoors, where people can better control their environment. Relief from smoke and heat is best when buildings have filtered air and climate control, and some communities provide public cleaner-air shelters for people whose buildings lack adequate filtration or cooling. In high heat, staying cool, hydrated and inside helps. Follow local emergency managers and public health officials on decisions to shelter in place. This advice concerns smoke, not approaching flames. If flames approach or the authorities order an evacuation, the evacuation order takes priority. Source: FEMA P-2055, Post-disaster Building Safety Evaluation Guidance (2019), PDF page 89. Origin of the sources: US. Audience: public. results.text: FI-17 Anticiper : débroussailler, stocker, adapter la maison. results.text: FI-02 Fires affect buildings unevenly, and damage may not be visible. After a fire or wildfire, some structures can be burned so badly that they are essentially destroyed while others are untouched, simply because of the path of the fire.
